entities.name: Adelir Antonio de Carli
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adelir Antonio de Carli (1963–2008) was a Brazilian Catholic priest who became internationally known — tragically — for his death during a fundraising balloon flight over the Atlantic Ocean in April 2008. A priest of the Diocese of Joinville in Santa Catarina, he had previously completed a balloon flight in 2006 using helium balloons to raise money for a chapel and a truck stop for truckers.

On 20 April 2008, Father Carli attempted a second balloon flight from Paranaguá in Paraná attached to approximately 1,000 helium party balloons. He had received some training but was not a certified balloon pilot. After drifting out to sea when his GPS device failed, contact was lost. His body was eventually found in pieces in the Atlantic Ocean in July 2008 by oil platform workers.

Father Carli's death became an international news story that generated both sympathy and dark humour. His pastoral motivation was genuine — he wanted to raise money for charitable causes connected to his ministry to truckers — but his lack of proper training and the inadequate risk assessment of the venture made the outcome a tragedy. His death became an example cited in discussions about clerical risk-taking and the limitations of good intentions without proper competence.
